current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024, 2025 and 2026 regular sessions. Codified Idaho Code Title 74 ch. 1 opened on legislature.idaho.gov (site states statutes are updated to the website July 1 following the legislative session, so the text read on 2026-08-19 reflects the 2026 session); § 74-102 history ends 'am. 2025, ch. 298, sec. 2' (H0253, 'Public records, requests, residents', eff. July 1, 2025 — created the resident/nonresident fee fork, the 21/35-day nonresident clocks in § 74-103, the resident-only waiver and the nonresident-fee itemization sentence). No 2024 amendment to § 74-102 (§ 74-103 was amended 2024 ch. 107). 2026 session: no fee/estimate bill on Title 74 became law (H0510/H0632 ethics, H0600/H0625/H0748 complaints-denials died in committee; H0894 open-meetings recording became law). No administrative rule binds municipalities on public-records fees; Idaho has no uniform state fee schedule and no delegation from § 74-102 to any rule-making instrument — every figure is set by the requested agency under the statutory 'actual cost' / lowest-paid-staff ceilings. Guidance-vs-law gaps: the AG Idaho Public Records Law Manual (July 2026) Q16 describes the fee waiver as one agencies are 'allowed to waive' and its reproduced § 74-102(10)(f) omits the 2025 words 'is a resident and'; the codified statute makes the waiver mandatory ('shall not charge') for residents who demonstrate the test. Statute governs.

resolutions.value: actual cost to the agency of copying the record (resident); actual costs of the public agency (nonresident)
resolutions.unit: USD per page (city-set under the standard)
resolutions.source_language: A public agency or public official may establish separate copying fee schedules for requests submitted by residents and requests submitted by persons who are not residents. The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record if another fee is not otherwise provided by law. | Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
resolutions.notes: Idaho sets no cents-per-page figure. Two regimes: residents (§ 74-101(15)) — fee may not exceed actual cost of copying, and the first 100 paper pages are free (ID-0018); nonresidents — rate and schedule at agency discretion, not to exceed actual costs. 'Public agency' = state or local agency (§ 74-101(8),(11)), so the standard binds cities directly. AG Legal Guideline 1/25/1993 (ID-9012): a city may not by ordinance charge above actual cost. City fee adoption is subject to the § 63-1311A hearing/notice procedure for new fees or >5% increases (applicability note). Statutes updated 7/1/2026 show no 2026 change.

resolutions.source_language: A public agency or public official may establish separate copying fee schedules for requests submitted by residents and requests submitted by persons who are not residents. The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record if another fee is not otherwise provided by law. | For providing a duplicate of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar or analogous record system containing public record information, a public agency or public official may charge a fee, uniform to all residents, that does not exceed the sum of the following: 1. The agency’s direct cost of copying the information in that form; 2. The standard cost, if any, for selling the same information in the form of a publication; 3. The agency’s cost of conversion, or the cost of conversion charged by a third party, if the existing electronic record is converted to another electronic form.

resolutions.source_language: Except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law, no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records that are requested by a resident.

resolutions.notes: Resident-only ('a request submitted by a resident'; resident defined § 74-101(15): 30-day continuous Idaho domicile, incl. domestic entities). Nonresidents get no free allotment (§ 74-102(10)(g), ID-9001). Carve-out: fees 'authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law' (e.g. recorder/court fees) are not displaced (ID-9013). Applies to 'public agency' = state and local agencies.

resolutions.value: per-hour pay rate of the lowest paid administrative staff employee or public official of the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the request (resident); nonresident: agency discretion not to exceed actual costs
resolutions.unit: USD per hour (city's own pay rate for that employee)
resolutions.source_language: Fees for requests made by residents shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred in responding to a public records request, and if charged, shall reflect the personnel and quantity of time that are reasonably necessary to process a request. Fees for requests made by residents for labor costs shall be charged at the per hour pay rate of the lowest paid administrative staff employee or public official of the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the request. If a request from a resident requires redactions to be made by an attorney who is employed by the public agency, the rate charged shall be no more than the per hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the public records request. If a request from a resident is submitted to a public agency that does not have an attorney on staff, and requires redactions by an attorney, the rate shall be no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney who is retained by the public agency for that purpose. | Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.

Only chargeable when § 74-102(10)(b) is met and after the free 2 hours (ID-0017, ID-9002).

resolutions.value: Resident: no charge for the first 2 hours of labor (and first 100 paper pages); fees to recover actual labor and copying costs may be established only if (i) request >100 pages of paper records, or (ii) records require deletion of nonpublic information, or (iii) actual labor exceeds 2 person-hours. Nonresident: labor and copying fees may be charged at agency discretion (≤ actual costs), no free allotment.
resolutions.source_language: Except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law, no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records that are requested by a resident. | A public agency or public official may establish fees to recover the actual labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents if: (i) The request is for more than one hundred (100) pages of paper records; or (ii) The request includes records from which nonpublic information must be deleted; or (iii) The actual labor associated with responding to requests for public records in compliance with the provisions of this chapter exceeds two (2) person hours. | Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.

resolutions.notes: Per request, resident-only; nonresidents receive no free labor (§ 74-102(10)(g)). Anti-splitting: agency may aggregate requests segregated to avoid fees (§ 74-102(11), ID-9005).

resolutions.source_language: A requester may not file multiple requests for public records solely to avoid payment of fees. When a public agency reasonably believes that one (1) or more requesters is segregating a request into a series of requests to avoid payment of fees authorized pursuant to this section, the public agency may aggregate such requests and charge the appropriate fees. The public agency may consider the time period in which the requests have been made in its determination to aggregate the related requests. A public agency shall not aggregate multiple requests on unrelated subjects from one (1) requester.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
resolutions.notes: Idaho's free allotment is per request, not per requester per period; there is no TX § 552.275-style periodic cap. The related control is aggregation of split requests (§ 74-102(11)). resolutions.source_language: The public agency shall not charge any cost or fee for copies or labor when the requester is a resident and demonstrates that the requester’s examination and/or copying of public records: (i) Is likely to contribute significantly to the public’s understanding of the operations or activities of the government; (ii) Is not primarily in the individual interest of the requester including, but not limited to, the requester’s interest in litigation in which the requester is or may become a party; and (iii) Will not occur if fees are charged because the requester has insufficient financial resources to pay such fees.

resolutions.value: Aggregation permitted: when the agency reasonably believes one or more requesters is segregating a request into a series to avoid fees, it may aggregate the requests and charge appropriate fees, considering the time period of the requests; it shall NOT aggregate multiple requests on unrelated subjects from one requester. No aggregation threshold or carry-forward rule.
resolutions.source_language: A requester may not file multiple requests for public records solely to avoid payment of fees. When a public agency reasonably believes that one (1) or more requesters is segregating a request into a series of requests to avoid payment of fees authorized pursuant to this section, the public agency may aggregate such requests and charge the appropriate fees. The public agency may consider the time period in which the requests have been made in its determination to aggregate the related requests. A public agency shall not aggregate multiple requests on unrelated subjects from one (1) requester.

new_rules.legal_concept: Nonresident fee rates and schedule at agency discretion, not to exceed actual costs
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may charge fees for labor and copying costs for requests by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident; the rates and schedule are at the agency's discretion as long as the fees do not exceed the agency's actual costs.

new_rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.

new_rules.legal_concept: Conditions under which labor and copying fees may be established
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may establish fees to recover actual labor and copying costs only if the request is for more than 100 pages of paper records, or includes records from which nonpublic information must be deleted, or the actual labor exceeds two person-hours.
new_rules.trigger: One of the three enumerated conditions is met
new_rules.source_language: A public agency or public official may establish fees to recover the actual labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents if: (i) The request is for more than one hundred (100) pages of paper records; or (ii) The request includes records from which nonpublic information must be deleted; or (iii) The actual labor associated with responding to requests for public records in compliance with the provisions of this chapter exceeds two (2) person hours.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: Gate on chargeability at all (labor.billableWhen). Disjunctive triggers. Interplay with (10)(a) free first 2 hours/100 pages for residents is not expressly reconciled.

new_rules.legal_concept: Itemized statement of fees; no lump sums; nonresident fees separately identified
new_rules.atomic_rule: Statements of fees shall be itemized to show per-page copy costs, hourly rates of employees and attorneys involved, and actual time spent; no lump-sum costs may be assigned; if a separate nonresident fee schedule is adopted, nonresident fees shall be separately identified.
new_rules.trigger: A public agency states fees for a request
new_rules.source_language: Statements of fees by a public agency shall be itemized to show the per page costs for copies, and hourly rates of employees and attorneys involved in responding to the request, and the actual time spent on the public records request. No lump sum costs shall be assigned to any public records request. If a separate fee schedule is adopted for requests from persons who are not residents or employees of residents, the separate fees for such nonresidents shall be separately identified.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: No dollar/hour threshold triggers the itemized statement; it applies whenever fees are stated. Nonresident-identification sentence added 2025 ch. 298.

new_rules.legal_concept: Attorney redaction labor rate ceilings (resident requests)
new_rules.atomic_rule: For a resident request requiring redactions by an agency-employed attorney, the rate charged shall be no more than the per-hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the agency who is necessary and qualified; if the agency has no attorney on staff, no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney retained for that purpose.
new_rules.trigger: Resident request; redactions performed by an attorney
new_rules.source_language: If a request from a resident requires redactions to be made by an attorney who is employed by the public agency, the rate charged shall be no more than the per hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the public records request. If a request from a resident is submitted to a public agency that does not have an attorney on staff, and requires redactions by an attorney, the rate shall be no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney who is retained by the public agency for that purpose.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: Split from ID-0020 (general lowest-paid-staff rate) so the attorney tier is its own ceiling. Nonresidents: agency discretion ≤ actual costs (ID-9001).

new_rules.legal_concept: Additional electronic-media duplication fees for nonresidents (uniform to nonresidents)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public agency may charge additional fees, uniform to all persons who are not residents, for requests involving duplication of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar record system.
new_rules.source_language: A public agency or public official may charge additional fees, uniform to all persons who are not residents, for requests involving duplication of a computer tape, computer disc, microfilm or similar or analogous record system containing public record information.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: Bounded by the actual-costs ceiling of (10)(g). Added 2025 ch. 298.

new_rules.legal_concept: After-hours examination: reasonable compensation of custodian's representatives, funded in advance by the requester
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian authorizes examination outside regular office or working hours, the persons designated to represent the custodian are entitled to reasonable compensation paid by the agency out of funds provided in advance by the person examining the records.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian authorizes examination outside regular hours
new_rules.source_language: In this event, the persons designated to represent the custodian during such examination shall be entitled to reasonable compensation to be paid to them by the public agency having custody of such records, out of funds provided in advance by the person examining such records, at other than regular office or working hours.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: Advance funding is mandatory for this service once authorized; the amount is 'reasonable compensation' (soft standard). AG Manual Q15 also cites advance payment for outside copying contractors/overtime.

new_rules.legal_concept: Recovery of actual mailing/telecommunications costs when asked to mail or fax records (AG guidance)
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to send records to a requester, but may recover actual mailing or telecommunications costs when asked to mail or fax records.
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks the agency to mail or fax records
new_rules.source_language: The law does not prevent the recovery of actual mailing or telecommunications costs if there is a request to mail or fax information to someone.
new_rules.source_authority: Idaho Attorney General, Idaho Public Records Law Manual (July 2026), Question No. 14
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: Guidance, not statute; Title 74 is silent on postage. Statute separately permits e-mail delivery (§ 74-102(4)). Preceding sentence of the answer: 'The law requires an agency to provide public records to members of the public; the agency is not required to send the records to the person making the request.'

new_rules.legal_concept: City may not by ordinance charge above actual cost of reproduction (AG Legal Guideline 1/25/1993)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A city may not pass an ordinance allowing it to charge a fee in excess of the actual cost of reproducing requested public records, notwithstanding the 'otherwise provided by law' language.
new_rules.source_language: Attorney General’s Legal Guideline, January 25, 1993 (city may not pass ordinance to allow it to charge a fee in excess of actual cost of reproducing requested public records despite the “otherwise provided by law” language of Idaho Code § 9-338(8)).
new_rules.source_authority: Attorney General’s Legal Guideline, January 25, 1993, as indexed in the Idaho Public Records Law Manual (July 2026), p. 69
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: The guideline itself was not opened; the source language is the manual's own summary (verbatim from the manual). Issued under former § 9-338(8), predecessor of § 74-102(10)(c). Municipal-specific.

new_rules.legal_concept: Fees authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law are preserved
new_rules.atomic_rule: The free-allotment rule and the actual-cost copying ceiling apply 'except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law' / 'if another fee is not otherwise provided by law'.
new_rules.trigger: Another Idaho statute prescribes a fee for the record (e.g. recorder, court records)
new_rules.source_language: Except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law, no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records that are requested by a resident. | A public agency or public official may establish separate copying fee schedules for requests submitted by residents and requests submitted by persons who are not residents. The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record if another fee is not otherwise provided by law.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
new_rules.notes: AG Manual Q13: exception 'preserve[s] fees already established by other laws, such as recorders’ fees and fees for court records.' No general municipal certified-copy or records fee statute found in Title 50; per AG Guideline 1993 (ID-9012) a city ordinance is not 'other law' for this purpose.

delegations_followed.instrument: None — statute contains no delegation to a rule, AG schedule, or uniform fee schedule; fee-setting is left to each public agency under the actual-cost / lowest-paid-staff ceilings
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: No delegated figures exist. Checked IDAPA for a general public-records fee rule binding local agencies (none; agency-specific schedules such as IDAPA 16.02.08.251 bind only that agency) and the AG manual for any published schedule (none).

delegations_followed.statute_cite: Idaho Code § 74-102(10)(a),(c) ('fees authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law')
delegations_followed.instrument: Other Idaho fee statutes (recorder, court) per AG Manual Q13; no municipal-records fee statute found in Title 50 ch. 9
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: None for municipal records; § 50-907(6)(c) makes a clerk-certified reproduction a certified copy but sets no fee.

applicability_notes: 'Public agency' means any state or local agency; 'local agency' expressly includes a city (§ 74-101(8),(11)) — every § 74-102(10)-(12) figure binds municipalities directly; there is no separate state-agency schedule.

Two requester regimes since 7/1/2025: residents (§ 74-101(15): 30-day continuous Idaho domicile, spouse/dependents, domestic entities; not workplace/vacation/part-time residence) get the free 2 hours/100 pages, the lowest-paid-staff labor ceiling, and the mandatory waiver; nonresidents (and persons not employed by a resident) get only the actual-costs ceiling with rates at agency discretion. Requesters must declare residency under oath in the request (§ 74-102(4)). Engine needs a residency flag driving the fee profile.

City fee adoption procedure (outside Title 74): § 63-1311 lets a taxing district impose fees 'reasonably related to, but ... not exceed[ing], the actual cost of the service' and § 63-1311A requires notice and a public hearing before imposing a new fee or increasing a fee more than 5%. Recorded as a note, not a request-handling rule.
AG Legal Guideline 1/25/1993 (via July 2026 manual): a city ordinance cannot set a records fee above actual cost of reproduction; municipal-specific.
AG manual guidance on postage/fax recovery (Q14) and on advance payment for after-hours/contractor/overtime work (Q15) is Official Guidance, not statute.
material_negatives: No statutory or regulatory cents-per-page copy rate, color/oversized/specialty rate, or graduated bands for any Idaho public agency — only the actual-cost ceiling.
No overhead/fringe percentage, no billing increment, no minimum fee, no de-minimis dollar amount.

No estimate threshold, requester response window, revision percentage, or estimate validity period; the only estimate-adjacent duties are the itemized fee statement (§ 74-102(10)(h)) and optional scope-narrowing help (§ 74-102(9)).

No deposit threshold or percentage cap; no nonpayment/withdrawal rule; no clock tolling while advance payment is outstanding; no overrun re-issue rule; nothing on electronic payment methods for records fees.
No certification fee, audio/video per-recording or per-minute fee, commercial-purpose schedule, periodic free-hours cap, or late-response fee forfeiture.
No administrative rule (IDAPA) or uniform fee schedule binding local agencies on public-records fees; § 74-102 delegates nothing.
